MCP Server
snippet:
# MCP Server
Access MrScraper’s web scraping API via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to enable AI agents to fetch and extract web data securely.
Use MrScraper’s web scraping API through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to let AI agents discover, fetch, and extract web data in real time. This cloud-hosted MCP server integrates directly with MrScraper, enabling secure, scalable scraping workflows without local setup or infrastructure management.

### Prerequisites
To use the MrScraper MCP server, you'll need:
1. [A MrScraper account](https://v3.app.mrscraper.com/auth/login)
2. [MrScraper Account API Key](/docs/getting-started/api-token#generating-an-api-token)
### Remote Hosted URL via HTTP Transport Protocol
The simplest way to use MrScraper MCP is through our remotely hosted server. No local installation required!

To connect the MrScraper MCP server in n8n:
1. In your n8n workflow, add an **AI Agent** node.
2. In the AI Agent configuration, add a new **Tool**.
3. Select **MCP Client Tool** as the tool type.
4. Enter the MCP server Endpoint:
1. Set **Server Transport** to **HTTP Streamable**.
2. Set **Authentication** to **None** (authentication is handled via API keys in tool calls).
3. For **Tools to include**, you can select **All**, **Selected**, or **All Except**.

title: hermes-agent/optional-mcps/mrscraper/manifest.yaml at b79e8e12ee1819bbbe4061439cf379853c505c28 · NousResearch/hermes-agent

description: Retrieve web pages, search Google, and check account usage.
source: https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server
# Official hosted Streamable HTTP server. Its 401 challenge advertises MCP
# protected-resource metadata and an OAuth authorization server with dynamic
# client registration and PKCE. No local package or static key is required.
transport:
type: http
url: https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
auth:
type: oauth
# The server currently exposes scraperAPI, webSearch, and status.
# With no fixed tool filter, installation lets
# users choose among the tools available at connection time.

On first connection, Hermes opens MrScraper browser sign-in. Approve access
and start a new session to load its tools. If sign-in does not start, run:
hermes mcp login mrscraper
The server provides scraperAPI (HTML, Markdown, or screenshots),
webSearch (Google results), and status (account usage and quota).
For managed scrapers, reruns, and stored results, use the MrScraper dashboard.
Review or change enabled tools with:
hermes mcp configure mrscraper
Requests send target URLs and search queries to
MrScraper's cloud service. Scraping and search can consume account tokens;
use status to inspect your remaining quota before large jobs.

title: Choose an Agent Framework for a Web Data Application
snippet:
- **The [MrScraper MCP server](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server).** It offers `scraperAPI`, `webSearch` and `status` tools to any MCP client. It runs hosted at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` or locally.
- **The [LangChain integration](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/integrations/langchain).** The `langchain-mrscraper` package gives LangChain and LangGraph agents eight ready-made tools.
- **The [REST API](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/overview), [Python SDK](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/integrations/python) or [Node.js SDK](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/integrations/node).** You wrap these in your own typed tools. Since every framework below supports MCP, the MCP server works with all of them. Custom tools give you more control over inputs, outputs and errors.

Here is the hosted MCP server in the OpenAI Agents SDK. The key comes from an environment variable and is sent as a bearer token, which is the API key option the MrScraper MCP docs describe.
python
```python
import os
from agents import Agent, Runner
from agents.mcp import MCPServerStreamableHttp
async def run_task(prompt: str):
async with MCPServerStreamableHttp(
name="mrscraper",
params={
"url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
"headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['MRSCRAPER_API_KEY']}"},
},
) as server:
agent = Agent(
name="Release checker",
instructions="Use only the given URLs. Quote the page for every field.",
mcp_servers=[server],
)
return await Runner.run(agent, prompt, max_turns=10)
```
And here is the same server in the Claude Agent SDK:
python
```python
import os
from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions
options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
mcp_servers={
"mrscraper": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
"headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['MRSCRAPER_API_KEY']}"},
}
},
allowed_tools=["mcp__mrscraper__scraperAPI"],
)
```

MrScraper is a developer-focused web data API. It provides a REST API, Python and Node.js SDKs, a LangChain integration and an MCP server with hosted and local options. These fetch pages, discover URLs and extract structured data, and each response reports usage.
Your application provides the framework, the model, the agent logic, state, limits, tracing and checks on the final answer. Your team also decides which sources it has permission to collect from.

title: Use MrScraper MCP to Compare Public SaaS Pricing and Plan Limits
snippet:
An MCP SaaS pricing comparison uses an AI client, such as Claude Code, to collect official pricing and help pages through MrScraper's MCP tools. The client then turns each page into structured, cited rows. You compare plans only where units match, and you mark every unpublished price or limit as unknown.

It works in four steps: you define the question, MrScraper MCP collects the official pages, your AI client extracts facts into a fixed schema, and you build the comparison from those facts. MCP handles collection. The comparison rules are yours, and they live in your prompt and your review.

MrScraper documents a hosted MCP endpoint at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` with OAuth 2.1 sign-in. In Claude Code, add it like this:
bash
```bash
claude mcp add \
--transport http \
--scope user \
mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```
Open `/mcp` in Claude Code to sign in. Other clients, including Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code, use the same URL. The [MrScraper MCP documentation](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server) lists the setup for each one.
